summary: The moving-section, uniform-density, signed-layer, Farkas-sign, and O(r_n)/o(r_n) arguments are sound on a compactified subsequence. The proof does not, however, promote the claimed limsup bound (3) to the full original sequence.
gaps: The compactified-subsequence argument yields (31), hence the ratio tends to at most zero, only along the chosen compactified subsequence. The final subsequence-removal paragraph argues only that infinitely many failures of the fixed bound (4) are impossible. That establishes eventual (4), whose constant 2/3 does not imply the stronger full-sequence conclusion limsup <= 0 in (3). The assertion immediately after (31) that division proves (3) therefore skips the required outer subsequence argument.
repair_hints: Apply compactification to a subsequence on which the normalized deficit is bounded below by some fixed positive epsilon: if the full-sequence limsup were positive, such a subsequence would exist, while (31) on a further compactified subsequence would force the normalized deficit to be o(1), a contradiction.
